marks.gloss_en: 'all work of goats' (Num 31:20) includes items that come from the goats -- from the horns and from the hooves
'and ALL work' amplifies: horn and hoof vessels of other domesticated and wild animals are also susceptible
the amplification 'and all work' would extend susceptibility to vessels from birds' bones as well
'עזים' -- goats: to exclude birds; vessels from birds' bones are not susceptible
bone vessels are susceptible to ritual impurity
מה תלמוד לומר וכל מעשה עזים תתחטאו? להביא דבר הבא מן העזים, מן הקרנים ומן הטלפים
שאר בהמה וחיה מנין? תלמוד לומר וכל מעשה
אין, דתניא: ... להביא דבר הבא מן העזים, מן הקרנים ומן הטלפים (kind svara: no plain דתניא citation kind)
a metal vessel still awaiting smoothing, inlay, planing, adorning, or hammering, or lacking a base, rim, or handle, is not susceptible
metal vessels are crafted for uses of honor, so they are not vessels until complete
the practical difference between the two reasons is bone vessels: expensive, but not crafted for honor
ואזדא רב נחמן לטעמיה, דאמר רב נחמן: כלי עצם ככלי מתכות דמו
ולמאן דאמר זה וזה לחיוב, גדולים למאי חזו? -- and for the one who says both to obligation, what are the large ones fit for?
הואיל ויכול למתקן על ידי האור -- since one can sweeten them by fire (= p_yachol_lematkan_baur)
R' Yochanan: since one can sweeten them by means of fire
bitter almonds, small -- obligated [in teruma and tithes]
R' Yosei (version 1): both this and that to exemption -- so the small [bitter] ones too are exempt
what is obligated in bitter almonds is exempt in sweet almonds
אי רבנן -- אף על גב דהחמיץ: for the Rabbis it is exempt even though it fermented, but the mishna treats fermented temed as fruit
אי רבי יהודה -- אף על גב דלא החמיץ: for R' Yehuda it is obligated even though it did not ferment, but the mishna treats unfermented temed as water
temed before it ferments -- [is it] bought with tithe money? (the mishna: it is NOT)
partner brothers: when they are obligated in the kalbon, they are exempt from animal tithe
one who makes temed, put in water by measure and found [only] its measure -- exempt [from tithing]
